OUR LITTLE CLASSROOMS

Science Lab

Ask a question. Follow your curiosity.

Grow a bean

Ages 6–1220 min + daily check-ins

Watch roots and shoots appear, then draw the changes in your own bean diary.

Sink or Float?

Ages 4–720–30 minutes

Test everyday objects in water, record what happens and redesign a foil boat.

My Weather Journal

Ages 4–75–10 minutes a day

Observe the sky, keep a weather diary, choose an outfit and build a toy shelter.

Shadow detectives

Ages 3–815 min

Torch in hand, children make shadows grow and shrink, turn them into creatures, predict their shapes and trace them like real evidence.

THE SCIENCE LAB SHELF · 53 FLASHCARDS

Fifty-three lab-equipment flashcards to download and print.

Every card names four real lab tools, drawn smiling and labeled for kids — from beakers and test tubes to microscopes, telescopes and the safety crew. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer. The pills answer one glance: the age, the subject, the grade level, the skill it builds — and anything hot, sharp or medical wears the Ask-a-grown-up badge.

TOOL TIME · 15 CARDS

The tools that hold, pour and measure.

Beakers and test tubes, flasks and funnels, rulers and scales, timers and magnifiers — the lab tools kids name first, drawn smiling and labeled clearly for little scientists.

STAY SAFE IN THE LAB · 7 CARDS

Grown-up gear, kid-sized rules.

Goggles and aprons, gloves and helmets, the emergency crew and the doctor tools — the safety cards that teach the biggest lab rule: ask a grown-up first. Anything sharp, hot or medical is a grown-up’s job.

LIGHT, SOUND & POWER · 8 CARDS

Sparks, wiggles and beams.

Circuits and batteries, magnets and meters, prisms and sound waves — the physics corner of the lab, where electricity travels in circles and sound travels in wiggles.

LIVING THINGS · 9 CARDS

From germs to giant trees.

Cells and DNA, leaves and seeds, butterflies and frogs, body models and food chains — the biology shelf for animal-loving kids and backyard nature walks.

EARTH, WEATHER & SPACE · 7 CARDS

Weather watchers and star counters.

Globes and maps, rain gauges and wind socks, fossils and planets — the earth-science shelf that turns a rainy sidewalk day into a weather station.

MACHINES & MOTION · 7 CARDS

The machines that push, spin and lift.

Pulleys and levers, centrifuges and solar ovens, atoms and telescopes — the physics-shelf machines that make things go.

HOW TO USE THE LAB CARDS

Point, name, then do the tiny version.

Pick one card and name the four tools out loud — the beaker wants to be called by name. Then find each tool’s job: the beaker holds, the thermometer reads, the goggles guard. Print the card and post it where the experimenting happens. Anything with the Ask-a-grown-up badge stays a grown-up tool — pointing and naming is always your job, and asking “what does this do?” is the whole habit of science.

What this room is for

The Science Lab turns kitchen-table questions into real experiments: a bean growing in a clear cup, objects that sink or float, a week of sky watching, shadows made with a torch. Each one follows the same honest loop — predict, test, write down what actually happened — which is the whole habit of science in one sitting.

How one session runs

Pick one experiment, gather the short materials list (seeds, a tub of water, a torch — nothing rare), and ask your child to guess out loud before every test. The printable diary sheets give them a place to record results, and “wrong” predictions are the best part: that is where the talking starts.
